title: Crash in [@ mozilla::dom::syncedcontext::Transaction<T>::Commit | mozilla::dom::BrowsingContext::SetOpenerPolicy ]
body:
+++ This bug was initially created as a clone of Bug #1823817 +++

The crash rate is looking better since bug 1823817, but there are still some remaining crashes with this signature.

(In reply to Andreas Farre [:farre] from bug 1823817 comment #30)
> We should probably look for missing security header processing on the JAR channel. I'm on PTO until Tuesday, so if we want to look before that I'd recommend adding the same (or similar) assert that we added in CallOnStartRequest.  Maybe start up a new bug for this?

Crash report: https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/05e29ab2-cb4f-4a54-b421-07a8f0230524

MOZ_CRASH Reason: ```CanSet failed for field(s): OpenerPolicy```

Top 10 frames of crashing thread:

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The one crash in desktop 103.0.2 is https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/6150ec53-e35a-478e-8396-1ddaa0230531
` 	CanSet failed for field(s): HasRestoreData `
So this is fixed on Desktop, the only remaining issues are on Android.

From what I can tell in bug 1823817 comment 26, the issue is with the PDF reader on android (does it work differently on android from desktop)? 
The reason it's in the JAR component is that the viewer is loaded from a resource URL [here](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/85b4f7363292b272eb9b606e00de2c37a6be73f0/toolkit/components/pdfjs/content/PdfStreamConverter.sys.mjs#1126,1194-1204) - I'm not sure if that afects how we set the openerPolicy - presumably it shouldn't since the listener still sees the original HTTP channel.

The other clue we have is that this is related to authentication.
I'm not sure if this is the case or not, but what could happen is that we load page X, get auth prompt, cancel auth, get OpenerPolicy 1, set it on the BC. Then we refresh, auth, get openerPolicy2, **attempt to set it on the same BC? **, hit the assertion because we fail [this condition](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/8dd0d2bebe4c897152da6c86d937e4be80bbaa54/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#3004-3011)
Andreas, do you think that's possible? The only question is why that would only happen on Android.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
(In reply to Valentin Gosu [:valentin] (he/him) from comment #3)
> The one crash in desktop 103.0.2 is https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/6150ec53-e35a-478e-8396-1ddaa0230531
> ` 	CanSet failed for field(s): HasRestoreData `
> So this is fixed on Desktop, the only remaining issues are on Android.

This must be the clue that explains the issue, I can't imagine a setup where there'd be no reports of a crash on desktop but loads on android where both platforms share an execution path. Not unless there is something that would be very racy, but even then I'd expect to see this on desktop as well. There's something androidy here that we just need to find.

> From what I can tell in bug 1823817 comment 26, the issue is with the PDF reader on android (does it work differently on android from desktop)? 
> The reason it's in the JAR component is that the viewer is loaded from a resource URL [here](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/85b4f7363292b272eb9b606e00de2c37a6be73f0/toolkit/components/pdfjs/content/PdfStreamConverter.sys.mjs#1126,1194-1204) - I'm not sure if that afects how we set the openerPolicy - presumably it shouldn't since the listener still sees the original HTTP channel.

To be honest, we highly suspect the PDF reader because we're loading a document from script that is in turn loaded from a JAR channel. This is all explained by a PDF being loaded. But it could be something we're missing.

> The other clue we have is that this is related to authentication.
> I'm not sure if this is the case or not, but what could happen is that we load page X, get auth prompt, cancel auth, get OpenerPolicy 1, set it on the BC. Then we refresh, auth, get openerPolicy2, **attempt to set it on the same BC? **, hit the assertion because we fail [this condition](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/8dd0d2bebe4c897152da6c86d937e4be80bbaa54/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#3004-3011)
> Andreas, do you think that's possible? The only question is why that would only happen on Android.

This would be very easily reproduced on desktop as well, and it would require a flip-flopping server once sending one set of Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy/Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy the other time another.

If we list the facts we have:

1) The `OpenerPolicy` for a `BrowsingContext` is initialized [on creation](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/8dd0d2bebe4c897152da6c86d937e4be80bbaa54/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#389-414)
2) Reloading a `BrowsingContext` will replace it with a new one, which means that it will have its `OpenerPolicy` again initialized as in step 1.
3) The browsing context is a top level context, otherwise we won't try to set the `OpenerPolicy` in [`Document::StartDocumentLoad`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/base/Document.cpp#3535-3540)
4) That `OpenerPolicy` cannot change from or to `OPENER_POLICY_SAME_ORIGIN_EMBEDDER_POLICY_REQUIRE_CORP` due to calling `BrowsingContext::SetOpenerPolicy`, because then [`BrowsingContext::CanSet(FieldIndex<IDX_OpenerPolicy>, ...)`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/8dd0d2bebe4c897152da6c86d937e4be80bbaa54/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#3004-3011) fails and we assert in [`Transaction<Context>::Commit`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/docshell/base/SyncedContextInlines.h#99-104).
5) From this it follows that the `OpenerPolicy` of the `BrowsingContext` and [`HttpBaseChannel::mComputedCrossOriginOpenerPolicy`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpBaseChannel.h#787) doesn't match.
6) `HttpBaseChannel::mComputedCrossOriginOpenerPolicy` is set in two places: [`HttpBaseChannel::ComputeCrossOriginOpenerPolicyMismatch`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpBaseChannel.cpp#2614) and [`HttpChannelChild::OnStartRequest`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpChannelChild.cpp#407). Skipping the first one was the root cause of bug 1823817, and that's fixed now.
7) For some reason there is always an nsJARChannel->Script->StartDocumentLoad stack
8) None of the crash reports have an URL
9) This happens exclusively on Android.

My reasoning goes like this, there are three possible explanations for 9:

1) Some resource only ever visited by Android devices cause the crash
2) There is a race 
3) There is an Android unique code path

1 seems unlikely to not have surfaced an URL in bug reports and 2 would at least give _some_ desktop crashes. So we end up in 3. And if pdf-js doesn't have a unique code path for Android then I'm leaning towards this being a Fission thing, since that's not enabled for Android. I threw a build on [try](https://treeherder.mozilla.org/jobs?repo=try&revision=ab9c27cda9b47ea5d7ac4b923ca63000c195344c) where I've turned off `fission.autostart` to see if this surfaces this on Desktop.

One thing I'm wondering about is if we're looking in the wrong place when it comes to `nsJARChannel`. Are there any more places where `nsJARChannel` would load some `.js[m]` that would in its turn load a document? That could be another way we'd do something Android specific.

Otherwise my thoughts go to `HttpChannelChild::OnStartRequest` and if it's possible that in a non-Fission context it's possible that due to a difference in async behaviour we get get to `HttpChannelChild::OnStartRequest` before processing headers in the parent?

Not sure if I've said anything new, but I wanted to summarize everything in one comment to make it easier to come back to or for someone else to start looking anew at this. If I've forgotten anything obvious please chime in.

(ni to :calixte and :valentin more to keep this ball rolling, please ni me if this shakes anything loose).

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
(In reply to comment #15)
> So in bug 1880240, they were able to run a mozregression and the most likely candidate is this:
> 
> https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1780614

That bug is the one which introduced the `CanSet` handler for the `OpenerPolicy` synced field, so even if there were issues before that patch, that patch is the one which would have added the ability to crash in this way.

In the case of bug 1880240 it sounds like the user is using enterprise policies to mark their internal site as "localfilelinks". I'm guessing that this corresponds to the `FileURIAllowList` (https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/a7e19af54ce40c7f2d0cb0457d3b12c279fe0f68/caps/nsScriptSecurityManager.cpp#1308). This is a super weird preference which allows specifying specific websites which should be loaded within the less-sandboxed `file` content process, and allowed to access the local filesystem. This pref effectively acts as an override on process selection, forcing all loads to end in the `file` content process.

It seems that there's an interesting interaction between this and the COOP+COEP headers. File URIs are not considered "cross-origin isolated", and there is no way to allow a file to use SharedArrayBuffer. In this case, I'm guessing the website is trying to use SAB (by setting COOP+COEP), while also being on the localfilelinks list. The localfilelinks list requires the URL to be in the `file` content process, while we need the page to be in a webCOOP+COEP= process to use SAB.

Process selection chooses that the file process requirement wins in this case, as it is necessary to avoid sandboxing violations. This leads to the process not going through the normal flow in `IsolationOptionsForNavigation` and not being put into a cross-origin isolated BrowsingContextGroup. The page will then not be properly isolated, and will end up hitting this assertion when networking code tries to set the COOP+COEP flags and isn't allowed to. I can post a patch to ensure that we finish the load in a cross-origin isolated BrowsingContextGroup in this case.

BTW, even once this is fixed, a site listed in `localfilelinks` will not be able to become "cross-origin isolated". This is because it needs to be loaded into a file content process, so it cannot be properly process-isolated.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Created attachment 9413631
Bug 1834864 - Select BCG more consistently during COOP+COEP process switches, r=participant8!


Previously it was possible to bypass specific BCG selection based on
cross-origin isolated status if the site was allowed to load file URIs
using enterprise policies, which could lead to a crash.

This patch changes the behaviour such that BCG selection now happens
correctly. The site will still not be cross-origin isolated due to being
loaded into a file content process.
